questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: These parking spaces are for people with disabled parking permits.
A roundabout is ahead.
Traffic in this lane must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.
These lanes are for buses and cars with a driver plus one or more passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: These parking spaces are for people with disabled parking permits.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that parking spaces are reserved for people with disabled parking permits.

questions.question: You can reduce the risk of hydroplaning by:

options.text: Driving through shallow water.
Driving faster.
Driving slower.
Driving through deep water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving slower.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast in wet conditions. Slowing down reduces the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light means:

options.text: The same as a stop sign.
The traffic light is broken.
You do not need to stop completely.
Driving conditions are very dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same thing as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A community group is picking up trash on the highway ahead.
Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
Children are playing ahead.
There is a pedestrian crosswalk ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that workers may be on or near the roadway ahead. Drive carefully through this area.

questions.question: Braking distance is affected by:

options.text: How fast your vehicle is going.
The condition of your brakes and tires.
The condition of the road.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Braking distance depends on your speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the road.

questions.question: When you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm out, you should:

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk your horn before passing the bus on the left.
Keep driving when you think most children have left the bus.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has its stop arm out, you must come to a complete stop. Do not move until the stop arm goes back in.

questions.question: You may park or stop on the freeway shoulder:

options.text: If you turn on your emergency flashers.
If no part of your vehicle touches the road.
If you need to check a map for directions.
Only in an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only in an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except in an emergency.

questions.question: How alcohol affects your reflexes and judgment:

options.text: Is less strong with beer than with wine.
Is less strong with wine than with beer.
Is strongest with hard ciders and mixed drinks.
Depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.correctAnswerText: Depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.
questions.explanation: All types of alcohol affect your reflexes and judgment the same way. What matters is the total amount of alcohol in your bloodstream, not the type of drink.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines mean you can pass another vehicle from either direction.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: FALSE
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot cross the center line to pass in either direction.

questions.question: You must yield to other drivers:

options.text: When leaving a garage or alley onto a street.
When another car is on your left at an unmarked intersection and you reach it at the same time.
When your traffic light is a green arrow.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When leaving a garage or alley onto a street.
questions.explanation: You must yield to other drivers when leaving a garage, driveway, or alley. You must also yield to pedestrians on an intersecting sidewalk.

questions.question: If a vehicle skids on water, the driver should quickly apply the brakes.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids while hydroplaning, try to regain control. If you cannot, release the accelerator and let the skid pass. Do not apply the brakes right away.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Steep downgrade.
Crossroad ahead.
No right turn.
Narrow bridge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downgrade.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert drivers to road conditions and hazards ahead. This sign warns you of a steep hill coming up. Slow down to protect your brakes and avoid accidents.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Continue at your current speed.
You must stop ahead.
Speeding is not allowed.
There is a traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a traffic signal is ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Signal before going any further.
Slow down and yield for trains.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield for trains.
questions.explanation: This sign indicates a railroad crossing ahead. Always slow down when approaching railroad tracks. Trains cannot move out of your way, so you must wait for them to pass before crossing.

questions.question: The most important thing to remember about speed and curves is that you must:

options.text: Drive at the posted speed limit as you enter the curve, then slow down at the sharpest part of the curve.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Accelerate gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the posted speed limit before, throughout, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle's inertia makes it hard to turn. To stay in control, slow down before entering a curve.

questions.question: A yellow light that flashes on and off means:

options.text: Stop and look for other vehicles, then go if there is no traffic.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: When turning left, drivers must yield the right-of-way to:

options.text: Other drivers who are already in the intersection.
Oncoming traffic.
Pedestrians who are already in the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic. Always yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to:

options.text: Vehicles in the roundabout.
Bicyclists in the roundabout.
Pedestrians in the roundabout.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: It is illegal for a person 21 years of age or older to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.05 percent.
0.08 percent.
0.02 percent.
0.1 percent.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent.
questions.explanation: For drivers 21 and older, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is illegal. Driving under the influence is dangerous and against the law.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Stop.
Start up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: A driver's left arm and hand extended downward means they are stopping. Adjust your driving if you are following a driver using this signal.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, what should you do?

options.text: Call the police right away.
Stay calm and move out of their way.
Flash your lights to show the driver they are wrong.
Do something aggressive back to get even.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of their way.
questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, stay calm and get out of their way. Trying to get even with them will make the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: At night, you can use parking lights instead of headlights.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You cannot drive at night using only parking lights. You must use your headlights when it is dark.

questions.question: What is true about emergency vehicles?

options.text: They have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and flashing lights.
They can use a loudspeaker to give instructions.
They can follow each other.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to police cars, fire trucks, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using a siren or horn and flashing lights. Follow any instructions from their loudspeakers. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so wait until the way is clear before moving.

questions.question: You are waiting in an intersection to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights so drivers will let you through.
Drive around a car that is blocking you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. If another car hits you from behind, straight wheels will keep you out of oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Slam on the brakes.
Hold the steering wheel tight and slow down to a stop.
Keep driving normally.
Turn on emergency flashers and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tight and slow down to a stop.
questions.explanation: Do not brake hard if your tire blows out. Grip the steering wheel firmly and stay in your lane. Slow down gradually by releasing the gas pedal. Once you are going very slowly, brake gently and pull off the road to a safe place.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop completely and go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are coming.
Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop, let others go first, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: Before turning, you should:

options.text: Use your turn signal.
Turn the wheel.
Speed up.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal.
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal 3 to 4 seconds before you turn.

questions.question: You are stranded in a snowstorm. What is the best thing to do?

options.text: Get out of the car and walk for help.
Lie down in your car and sleep.
Walk into the road to get other drivers' attention.
Stay in your car so people can find you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car so people can find you.
questions.explanation: If you are stranded in a snowstorm, stay in your car and wait for help. People are more likely to find you if you stay in your vehicle. Walking around in a snowstorm is unsafe.

questions.question: When can you use your horn?

options.text: When you have to stop quickly.
When you are passing another car.
When you lose control of your car.
When you are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you lose control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. This warns other drivers of danger.

questions.question: What happens if a bicyclist breaks traffic laws?

options.text: Bicyclists do not have to follow traffic laws.
They can receive a ticket.
They will always get a warning.
Their bicycle will be taken away.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can receive a ticket.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as car drivers. Both can receive tickets for breaking traffic laws.
